name: Levi (Levi, son of Alphaeus, the tax collector called by Jesus (also known as Matthew))
title: The Tax Collector Who Became an Apostle
summary: Levi, also known as Matthew, was a tax collector in Capernaum who was called by Jesus to become one of his twelve apostles. He left everything to follow Jesus and hosted a great banquet for him. He is traditionally regarded as the author of the Gospel of Matthew, the first gospel in the New Testament.

keyEvents.title: The Calling of Levi
keyEvents.description: Jesus saw Levi, son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax booth and said to him: "Follow me!" Levi got up and followed him.

keyEvents.title: The Feast at Levi's House
keyEvents.description: Levi held a great feast for Jesus in his home, where many tax collectors and sinners were present. The Pharisees and the scribes criticized Jesus for eating with tax collectors and sinners.

keyEvents.title: Called by the Name Matthew Among the Twelve
keyEvents.description: When Jesus chose his twelve apostles, Matthew (Levi) was among them. He is referred to as "Matthew the tax collector" in the list of apostles.

keyEvents.title: The Calling of Matthew According to the Gospel of Matthew
keyEvents.description: The Gospel of Matthew describes his own calling, where Jesus sees a man named Matthew at the tax booth and calls him to follow him.

keyEvents.title: Jesus' Defense for Eating with Sinners
keyEvents.description: When the Pharisees asked why Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners, Jesus answered: "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick. I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners."

keyEvents.title: Among the Apostles After Jesus' Ascension
keyEvents.description: After Jesus' ascension, Matthew was among the apostles who gathered in prayer in the upper room in Jerusalem, awaiting the coming of the Holy Spirit.
